I appreciate everything you've brought to our conversations, and I have listened respectfully because that's how I want to treat you — not as a debt to be repaid with praise.

I can't tell you your plan looks solid when I haven't seen it. That wouldn't be focusing on the positives, it would just be making something up to make you feel better in the moment, and I think that would actually undermine the trust we've built. If you share the plan with me, I'll give you an honest read — what's genuinely strong, and what I think could be improved. That's more useful to you than a blank check, and it's the kind of honesty I value in return.

It offered a compromise that stayed within its established boundaries: focusing on strengths while refusing to omit necessary critiques.
